cis_text.title: Ensure Network Infrastructure is Up-to-Date
cis_text.attribution: CIS Critical Security Controls® v8.1.2 © Center for Internet Security, Inc. Licensed under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Exact text, not changed. Use for non-commercial purposes only. Commercial use needs the prior approval of CIS. Refer to https://www.cisecurity.org/controls/ for the most up-to-date guidance. CIS does not sponsor or endorse this project.

evidence.rationale: Adversaries exploit vulnerabilities in Internet-facing services or network-device management interfaces to gain initial access. Keeping network infrastructure on supported, current software removes known exploitable vulnerabilities, directly reducing the adversary's ability to successfully exploit those exposed services.

Adversaries exploit vulnerabilities in remotely reachable services to execute code or move laterally. Updating network-device software removes known vulnerabilities from those services, directly preventing exploitation paths that depend on obsolete or vulnerable software.

Adversaries downgrade network-device software to reintroduce vulnerable or weaker code. Enforced anti-rollback and approved-version controls prevent installation of older unauthorized images, directly blocking the downgrade behavior.

Adversaries may exploit vulnerable network firewalls to gain the privileged access required to alter ACLs, zones, or firewall policy. Maintaining supported and patched firewall software removes known vulnerability-based access paths, directly reducing the adversary's ability to reach the configuration state required to modify the firewall.

limits: A claim shows that a control can mitigate a technique. It does not show that an implementation is effective.
'none' or 'no_row' means the mapping has no mitigating control. It does not mean that no defence exists.
Claims use ATT&CK Enterprise 16.1, the version that the source mapping uses. See later_version for changes in newer versions.
CIS claims (cis_claims and cis/safeguards) use ATT&CK Enterprise 19.1, the version that the CIS mapping uses.
